body.p: Claims 1-30 have been previously cancelled. Claims 31, 37, 38, 42, 48, and 49 have been amended. No new matter has been added. Thus, claims 31-51 are pending in the present application. In view of the above amendments and the following remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that all of the presently pending claims are in condition for allowance.
Claims 31-51 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as directed to an abstract idea without significantly more.

Amended claim 31 recites a method for non-invasive determination of a hemodynamic parameter of a subject mechanically ventilated via a breathing apparatus based on a point in time, thb, of a heartbeat of the subject and an arrival point in time, tarrpulm, at which a blood pressure pulse caused by the heartbeat reaches lungs of the subject, comprising "determining the point in time, thb, of the heartbeat of the subject based on blood oxygenation data measured via a blood oxygen sensor" and "obtaining a respiratory pressure and/or a respiratory flow via one of a pressure sensor and a flow sensor of the breathing apparatus" along with "determining, via a controller of the breathing apparatus, tarr_pulm from a change in the measured respiratory pressure and/or the respiratory flow resulting from a change in lung volume caused by the arrival of the blood pressure pulse to the lungs" and "determining, via the controller, a pulmonary pulse transit time, PTTpulm, for the blood pressure pulse based on thb and tarr_pulm" and "determining, via the controller, the hemodynamic parameter based on PTTpulm." Support for the amendment may be found at least on p. 24, I. 9-p. 25, I. 2 of the Specification.
It is respectfully submitted that amended claim 31 satisfies the requirements of

patentability and is thus allowable over 35 U.S.C. § 101. According to MPEP 2106, the claimed invention must qualify as patent-eligible subject matter - i.e., the claim must not be directed to a judicial exception (step 2A) unless the claim as a whole includes additional imitations amounting to significantly more than the exception (step 2B).

Step 2A is a two-prong analysis: 1) whether the claim recites an abstract idea, law of nature, or a natural phenomenon, and 2) whether the claim recites additional elements that integrate the judicial exception into a practical application. With respect to the first prong of analysis, the Examiner contends that the claim recites an abstract idea and, in particular,

mathematical relationships/calculations and/or mental process. Applicant maintains that a claim does not recite a mathematical concept if it is only based on or involves a mathematical concept. MPEP 2106.04(a)(2) states that "a limitation that is merely based on or involves a mathematical concept described in the specification may not be sufficient to fall into this grouping, provided that the mathematical concept itself is not recited in the claim." Indeed, the pulmonary pulse transit time is recited as being based on the point in time of the heartbeat and the arrival point in time of the arrival blood pressure pulse to the lungs and the hemodynamic parameter is recited as being based on the pulmonary transit time. Applicant notes that the claim has been amended to further recite the step of "determining the point in time, thb, of the heartbeat of the subject based on blood oxygenation data measured via a blood oxygen sensor". The Examiner contends that words used in a claim operating on data to solve a problem can serve the same purpose as a formula. It is respectfully submitted, however, that none of the recited claim limitations express either via formula or words any mathematical relationship or concept. While the Examiner suggests that such language may, alternatively, be indicative of a mental process, Applicant respectfully disagrees. It is respectfully submitted that the claim limitations cannot practically be performed via the human mind. In particular, the limitation of "determining the point in time, thb, of the heartbeat of the subject based on blood oxygenation data measured via a blood oxygen sensor" requires more than mere observation and/or generic evaluation of blood oxygenation data to determine the point in time, thb, of the heartbeat of the subject based thereon. As will be understood by those of skill in the art and as supported by the Specification, a blood oxygen sensor is conventionally used to measure and/or monitor the oxygen content or concentration of a subject's blood during ventilation. See Specification, p. 20, Il. 33-34. A point in time of a heartbeat is not readily identifiable from observation of blood oxygenation data. Thus, it is respectfully submitted that the claim limitations do not recite an abstract idea.
Even if the claim could be determined as reciting an abstract idea, it is respectfully

submitted that any purported judicial exception is integrated into a practical application and is thus not directed to a judicial exception under prong 2 of the analysis. The purported exception is implemented with or used in conjunction with a particular machine or manufacture that is integral to the claim - i.e., a breathing apparatus of a ventilation system. See MPEP 2106.05(b). The Examiner contends that the breathing apparatus of the ventilation system of the recited claim utilizes a generic computer that is used in a routine or customary way, in which there is no improvement or change in the function of the device. The Examiner contends that

the sensors are merely associated with data gathering steps for insignificant extra-solution activity. Applicant respectfully disagrees. It is respectfully submitted that the recited blood oxygen sensor, in particular, is not being utilized in a generic fashion according to a conventional breathing apparatus. As noted above, a blood oxygen sensor, when used in conjunction with a conventional breathing apparatus, is used to monitor a subject's blood oxygen concentration during ventilation. In the recited claim, however, the blood oxygen sensor, and its corresponding data, is utilized to determine a point in time of a heartbeat of the subject. It is respectfully submitted that the blood oxygen sensor according to the recited claim clearly does not conform to a generic and/or conventional usage thereof. Thus, it is respectfully submitted that there is a clear change in the function of the breathing apparatus of the recited claim such that the purported abstract idea is integrated into a practical application.

Furthermore, at the very least, under Step 2B, it is respectfully submitted that the claim includes additional elements amounting to significantly more than the purported judicial exception. The steps of the recited claim are more than mere data gathering of insignificant extra-solution activity according to MPEP 2106.05(g). As noted above, the limitations of the claim are applied via a particular machine and provide clear improvement/change in the function of the machine (e.g., breathing apparatus). As further evidenced via the lack of prior art, non- invasive determinations of arrival point in time of blood pressure pulses based to the lung based on respiratory pressure/flow, and pulse transit times determined therefrom, as recited in the claim, is a new, inventive concept. The Specification clearly differentiates between pulmonary flow induced measurements, as recited in the claim, and traditionally obtained systemic measurements. Thus, it is submitted that the claim provides more than mere data collection and includes an inventive concept - significantly more - such that the claims are allowable over 35 U.S.C. 101.

Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that claim 31 is allowable over 35 U.S.C. § 101 and that the rejection of this claim should be withdrawn. Because claims 32-40 depend from and include all of the limitations of claim 31, it is respectfully submitted that these claims are also allowable.
Claims 41 and 42 recite limitations substantially similar to the limitations of claim 31. Thus, for at least the same reasons as discussed above with respect to claim 31, it is
respectfully submitted that claims 41 and 42 are allowable over 35 U.S.C. § 101 and that the
rejection of these claims should be withdrawn. Because claims 43-51 depend from and include all of the limitations of claim 42, it is respectfully submitted that these claims are also allowable.
Claims 31-51 have been provisionally rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as unpatentable over claims 45-69 of copending U.S. Patent Application Serial No.

Applicant respectfully disagrees with the rejection. It is respectfully submitted, however, that Applicant is prepared to file a Terminal Disclaimer, if necessary, once the above-referenced rejections have been overcome.
In view of the foregoing, it is respectfully submitted that all of the currently pending
claims are in condition for allowance. All issues raised by the Examiner having been addressed, an early and favorable action on the merits is earnestly solicited.
Respectfully submitted,
